subject: Urgent: Streaming timeouts & retry storms impacting AvaLytics — immediate mitigation plan
messages:
From: Ava Cloud <ava@avalytics.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-15T09:12:00Z
Subject: Major streaming failures and timeouts (urgent)

Marissa —

We're seeing a large increase in 5xx and 429 responses for streaming/chat completions since ~02:00 PDT. Clients report idle stream disconnects (partial transcripts) and frequent client-side timeouts that force repeated reconnects. The error rate spike coincides with a burst of retries from our web clients — we now have multiple customers reporting degraded chat UX.

Sample symptoms:
- ~18% of streaming requests return HTTP/2 stream reset or 5xx before final tokens
- Several 429 bursts followed by retry storms from our front-end (we log exponential reconnect attempts)
- Idle streams disconnecting after ~28–32s with no trailing tokens (client SDK v2.1)

We attached a short capture of error traces and timestamps (streaming-error-samples.txt). This is customer-facing and hitting SLAs. Please escalate — we need an immediate mitigation and an RCA.

Ava Cloud
Head of Product Operations
ava@avalytics.com

--
Attachment: streaming-error-samples.txt (text)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Ava Cloud <ava@avalytics.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-15T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Major streaming failures and timeouts (urgent)

Hey Ava — thank you for the fast heads-up and the logs. I'm escalating to our SREs and product leads (cc'd). We own this and will provide an action plan within 30 minutes. Preliminary asks while we investigate:

1) If possible, push clients to pause aggressive reconnects (add a 5–10s static delay) to avoid amplifying 429s.
2) If streaming UX is critical, we can flip your workspace to non-streaming completions temporarily to avoid partial transcripts while we stabilize.

Vivek — can you triage SRE and confirm whether this is an SDK-side/retry pattern or a server-side resource saturation? Hannah/rachel — I'll need a suggested customer credit if this crosses SLA thresholds.

I attached our initial notes. I'll update in the next 15–30m.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Attachment: initial_analysis_notes.md (markdown)
From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-15T09:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Major streaming failures and timeouts (urgent) — SRE triage notes

Short summary of what we see (live):
- Gateway metrics: spike in connections with heavy short-lived reconnects starting 02:07 PDT; per-connection token rate remained normal but aggregate RPS spiked by ~6x for a specific subset of user agents.
- Rate limiter behavior: we saw transient 429s from the gateway which cascaded to upstream workers (queues backed up). Once a client receives 429, many clients retry immediately (SDK v2.1 has aggressive backoff defaults for reconnects), creating a retry storm.
- Streaming specifics: HTTP/2 streams were getting reset around 28–33s when upstream worker pools were stretched; idle-stream timeout in the gateway is currently 30s which is too aggressive under degraded conditions.

Immediate mitigations we can push in the next 20–40m:
1) Increase gateway idle-stream timeout from 30s -> 90s to avoid premature disconnects while we drain backlog.
2) Temporarily enable per-account connection rate limiting to smooth bursts for AvaLytics.
3) Deploy a gateway header that encourages clients to use exponential jittered backoff (we can set Retry-After heuristics).
4) Provide a toggle to fall back to non-streaming completions for their workspace if streaming remains unreliable.

I'll start a hotfix branch for the gateway timeout change and coordinate a canary deploy. Preliminary RCA points to a combined client-side aggressive reconnect pattern + gateway backpressure.

Vivek Kulkarni
SRE Lead — Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Attachment: sre_snapshot_09_35.json (monitoring snapshot)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Ava Cloud <ava@avalytics.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-15T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Major streaming failures and timeouts (urgent) — mitigation plan and timeline

Ava — quick update and proposed mitigation path:

- We've identified retry storms from a subset of SDK users as the triggering factor; gateway idle-streams are too short under load.
- Immediate actions (starting now):
  • Canary deploy to increase gateway idle-stream timeout 30s -> 90s (will reduce premature disconnects).
  • Enable per-account smoothing for AvaLytics to limit burst RPS.
  • Offer to switch your workspace to non-streaming completions for the next 2 hours while we stabilize; this preserves correctness at the cost of longer TTFB.

We expect the canary to show improvement within ~20 minutes. If you agree, we'll flip your workspace to non-streaming now and schedule a 30-minute sync to walk through logs and credit compensation.

We will follow up with an RCA and formal SLA credit proposal. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your customers.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Two asks:
1) Please document the RCA (we will need it for our internal incident log).
2) We expect SLA credits for the impacted window; Procurement is looped on this thread (procure@avalytics.com).

We are available for a 30-minute sync at 11:15 PDT if that works.

Ava Cloud

Subject: Re: Major streaming failures and timeouts (urgent) — final update and next steps

Ava — final update from our side:
- Canary deploy completed at 11:02 PDT; gateway idle-stream timeout increased to 90s and per-account smoothing enabled. Post-deploy monitoring shows 5xx/429 rates returned to baseline within ~40 minutes.
- We switched your workspace to non-streaming during the window; we have traffic logs and the SRE snapshot attached.
- Next steps:
  • We will deliver an RCA doc by EOD tomorrow (including root cause, timeline, and recommended SDK patches).
  • Our billing team will produce an SLA credit proposal; Rachel will follow up on compensation.
  • Vivek's team will harden gateway backpressure behavior and ship an SDK guidance note for exponential jittered backoff.

For exec visibility, Hannah has the incident brief and can escalate if you need further commercial remediation. Thank you for your patience — we know this was disruptive.
